label: accepted

evidence.V1: Lumpy faceted mass with a mossy top reads as a boulder in front, three-quarter and silhouette; top view still reads as rock (with a small pebble). Readable at 64 px.
evidence.V2: Only some hierarchy: one big mass, moss cap and a small pebble that is hidden behind the boulder in front/three-quarter views; facets are all similar size with no cracks, ledges or chips.
evidence.V3: Facets are arranged as a very regular table / crown / girdle ring, so the boulder reads like a cut gemstone rather than a weathered stylised rock; partly stylised.
evidence.V4: Consistent thin chamfers along the girdle and facet edges catch light in the side-facets close-up; no razor edges.
evidence.V5: Top and side close-ups in studio light show faint diagonal triangulation streaks across the large grey facets (smoothing across split quads); minor.
evidence.V6: Stone grey in two/three values plus moss green; disciplined with good contrast; redrock/slate colourways keep the scheme.
evidence.V7: 308 tris vs rock target 400 (ceiling 1000): under target.
evidence.V8: One vertex-colour material, designed flat facets with chamfers, stone + moss palette: matches the nature kit.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Anchored, Hull collision, CanTouch off, MeshPart.Color white, SmoothPlastic, origin bottom-centre: correct.

evidence.V1: Chunky faceted boulder outline reads as a rock from front, three-quarter, top and silhouette.
evidence.V2: Big mass and medium tier (designed facets, moss cap) are clear; the only small element, a side pebble, is visible in the top view only and hidden in front/three-quarter.
evidence.V3: Low faceted dome with a flat moss crown reads somewhat like a bevelled polyhedron; mass is plausible but not pushed (no lean, overhang or wedge character).
evidence.V4: Designed flat facets with soft narrow chamfers; highlight catches consistently along facet edges in the side-facets close-up.
evidence.V5: Studio and flat close-ups are clean: flat facets, no pinches, seams or z-fighting; moss boundary follows facet edges crisply; 0 flipped faces, A17/A18 pass.
evidence.V6: One stone hue in light/dark values plus one moss green secondary; colourways (sandstone, basalt with teal moss) keep the same two-material discipline.
evidence.V7: 308 tris vs rock target 400 - under target.
evidence.V8: Single LF_VertexColor material, designed rock facets, stone + leaf-green moss secondary exactly as the Nature spec describes.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Anchored, Hull collision, CanTouch off, MeshPart.Color white, SmoothPlastic, origin bottom-centre.

evidence.V1: Reads as a mossy boulder from front, 3/4, top and silhouette: low faceted mass with an irregular polygonal outline and a green cap; a small companion pebble appears in the top view.
evidence.V2: Big mass and small moss cap/pebble are present, but the medium tier is thin: the body is a single shell of ~10 broad facets with no ledges, cracks or secondary lumps.
evidence.V3: Proportions are a nice low wide boulder (5.8 x 6.3 x 2.8 studs), but the top is a regular radial facet fan around a flat moss plateau, so it reads somewhat like a cut gem rather than a natural stylised rock.
evidence.V4: Designed flat facets with consistent soft chamfered borders; facet edges catch a gentle highlight uniformly (side-facets and top close-ups).
evidence.V5: Clean shading in studio and flat close-ups; no pinches, seams or z-fighting (0 cross-shell overlaps).
evidence.V6: Stone grey in 3 values (light top, mid, dark base) plus one moss green; redrock and slate colourways stay disciplined.
evidence.V8: One white vertex-colour material, stone hue + moss secondary, designed flat facets with small chamfers - matches the nature kit.
evidence.V9: Anchored, Hull collision, CanTouch off, SmoothPlastic, MeshPart.Color white, origin bottom-centre.

artifacts: Faint triangulation streaks across large facets in studio light
top_fixes: Break the gem-cut regularity: vary facet sizes and angles, tilt the top plane, add one stepped ledge or crack
Move the companion pebble to the front/side so it reads in the main views (or drop it)
Mark the large facets flat-shaded / split normals so the triangulation streaks disappear
Push the form: tilt or wedge the mass with one dominant overhanging face so it reads less like a regular faceted dome
Move the side pebble (or add a second) where it shows in front and three-quarter views to give a visible small tier
Let the moss drip a little down one side instead of a flat polygon cap
Break the radial facet symmetry on top (irregular facet sizes, tilt the moss plateau) so it reads less like a cut gem
Add a medium tier: a ledge, a split, or a second fused lump on one side
Let the moss drape slightly over one edge instead of sitting as a flat polygon cap
Make the companion pebble visible from the front/3-4 views or remove it
